reading.title: IELTS Academic Unit 01 — Education: Reading
reading.description: 原创 IELTS-style 学术阅读篇章（7 段），配 15 题练习。
paragraphs: Education has traditionally been associated with the transfer of knowledge from teachers to students. In a conventional classroom, teachers explain concepts, students take notes, and examinations are used to measure what students have learned. Although this model remains common, the role of education has gradually expanded. Modern education is increasingly expected to prepare learners not only to remember information but also to use knowledge effectively in changing circumstances.

One important change concerns access to education. In many societies, higher education was once available mainly to a relatively small proportion of the population. Universities were often regarded as institutions for students who had achieved particularly strong academic results. Today, participation in higher education has expanded, and a wider range of learners seek university qualifications. At the same time, vocational education and professional training provide alternative routes for people who want to develop specific practical skills.

This expansion has created new questions about the purpose of education. A qualification can demonstrate that a person has completed a particular programme, but employers and other organisations may also expect graduates to communicate effectively, solve problems and work independently. Consequently, educational institutions increasingly consider learning outcomes that go beyond the simple accumulation of information.

Another major development is the use of digital technology. Online courses, recorded lectures and digital resources can give learners access to educational materials without requiring them to be physically present on a university campus. This flexibility can be particularly useful for people who work, live far from educational institutions or have other responsibilities. However, digital learning does not automatically produce better educational outcomes. Learners still need appropriate resources, clear instruction and sufficient motivation to participate effectively.

Assessment is also changing. Traditional examinations remain important, but educators increasingly use different forms of assessment to understand how students are progressing. Projects, presentations, practical tasks and continuous assessment can provide information that a single examination may not reveal. These approaches can evaluate not only what learners know but also how they apply their knowledge.

Another increasingly important idea is lifelong learning. Changes in technology and employment mean that knowledge and professional skills may need to be updated repeatedly. A qualification obtained early in a person’s career may not provide all the knowledge required decades later. Lifelong learning therefore treats education as an ongoing process rather than something that ends when a person leaves school or university.

The changing role of education does not mean that traditional teaching methods have become irrelevant. Teachers remain important because they provide guidance, explain difficult concepts and help learners evaluate information. Technology can support these activities, but it does not remove the need for effective teaching. The future of education is therefore likely to involve a combination of established educational practices and new approaches that give learners greater access, flexibility and responsibility.

exercise.title: IELTS Academic Unit 01 — Education: Practice
exercise.itemTitle: IELTS Academic Unit 01 — Education: Practice Set
exercise.description: Multiple Choice ×5、True/False/Not Given ×5、Vocabulary in Context ×5，含答案与解析。

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Universities should replace traditional examinations with digital learning.
Education is changing from a mainly knowledge-transfer model towards a broader and more flexible role.
Online education is more effective than classroom education.
Vocational education is becoming more important than university education.

questions.explanation: The passage discusses several changes in education, including access, skills, technology, assessment and lifelong learning. It does not argue that one particular method should replace all others.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, what has happened to participation in higher education?

options.text: It has become restricted to students with exceptional academic results.
It has expanded to include a wider range of learners.
It has been replaced by vocational training.

questions.explanation: The passage states that participation in higher education has expanded and that a wider range of learners now seek university qualifications.

questions.prompt: Why does the passage say that a qualification may not be enough for employers?

options.text: Employers may also require communication, problem-solving and independent-working skills.
Universities no longer teach practical subjects.
Employers prefer vocational qualifications in every situation.

questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 states that organisations may expect graduates to communicate, solve problems and work independently in addition to holding a qualification.

questions.prompt: What limitation of digital learning is mentioned?

options.text: Digital resources are unavailable to most learners.
Digital technology alone does not guarantee better learning outcomes.
Online courses are only useful for university students.

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that digital learning does not automatically produce better educational outcomes.

questions.prompt: What does the final paragraph suggest about the future of education?

options.text: Education will probably combine established practices with newer approaches.
Students will become entirely responsible for their own education.

questions.explanation: The final paragraph argues for a combination of established educational practices and new approaches.

questions.prompt: Higher education was historically available to a relatively small proportion of the population.
Most employers consider university qualifications more important than practical skills.
questions.explanation: The passage says employers may expect graduates to communicate, solve problems and work independently, but it does not compare the relative importance of qualifications and practical skills.

questions.prompt: Digital learning automatically produces better educational outcomes.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that digital learning does not automatically produce better educational outcomes.

questions.prompt: Projects and presentations can provide information that a single examination may not reveal.
questions.explanation: This is stated directly in paragraph 5.

questions.prompt: The passage claims that lifelong learning should become compulsory for all workers.
questions.explanation: The passage explains why lifelong learning is increasingly important but does not state that it should be compulsory.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 1, what does “conventional” most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: “Conventional classroom” refers to the established or traditional classroom model described immediately afterwards.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 3, what does “accumulation” most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: “Accumulation of information” means gradually collecting information.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 4, what does “flexibility” refer to?

options.text: The ability to change a university's curriculum every year
The ability to study without any instruction
The ability to fit learning around different circumstances

questions.explanation: The paragraph connects flexibility with people who work, live far away or have other responsibilities.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 5, what does “reveal” most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: An examination may fail to “reveal” certain information, meaning it may fail to show it.

questions.prompt: In the final paragraph, what does “established educational practices” most nearly refer to?

options.text: Methods that have already been accepted and used in education

questions.explanation: “Established” means already accepted or recognised; the phrase contrasts established practices with newer approaches.
